reasons.plausibility: Graphene coatings can delaminate or oxidize above ~200°C, and the hypothesis does not address adhesion to the HEA or how the coating survives the stated 200°C upper bound, making the mechanism questionable for the full temperature range.
reasons.testability: The proposed comparative tribological test with clear metrics and a falsification criterion is straightforward and feasible, though the temperature range (-20 to 200°C) and load (up to 1000 N) are specified.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is too generic (graphene coating on an unspecified HEA) and ignores known temperature limitations of graphene, so it offers little actionable guidance for a researcher working on self-lubricating HEAs across a wide temperature range.
